It’s been getting worse over the last 4–5 months. Since my husband died a few years ago I’ve been low, but lately it feels like it’s sunk to a different level. I wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning and just lie there, staring at the ceiling, thinking “what’s the point.” I don’t enjoy my knitting group or church anymore; I mostly stay in the house. Some days I don’t even bother to change out of my nightgown.

My appetite has really dropped off. I’m not purposely avoiding bread or meat or anything like that; food just doesn’t appeal to me. I’ll look at the plate and feel tired, and I only manage a few bites. My daughter keeps saying I’m too thin and is worried, but I just sort of shrug. It’s not that I’m trying to lose weight or scared of getting fat—I honestly don’t care either way. I’m just so tired, in my body and in my head, and I feel like a burden. Even simple things like paying bills or watering the plants feel overwhelming.

    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
